parsed.explanation: No anti-trans statute, no arrest pattern, no police targeting and no facility, care or employment ban are documented; the operative document is the home passport, and the state neither criminalises nor frames trans people as a threat — senior officials endorse Pride and the head of state has publicly backed it. Set against that: no gender-identity coverage in hate-crime or general non-discrimination law, no documented enforcement of the sectoral protections in any trans case, reported verbal abuse and discrimination in some public services including medical centres, family/community-based violence, and closed partnership recognition. The traveller's worst documented exposure is tier-3 societal hostility with thin recourse, not a state-imposed universal measure; border and screening practice is simply undocumented, an open question rather than a shown exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border or security-screening practice for trans travellers, no document-marker flagging, no recorded refusal or secondary-inspection pattern; treatment of a passport marker differing from presentation is unsourced.
entry_documents.protection: The home-issued passport or ID card, including any marker changed abroad, is the operative document; no domestic marker procedure is required of a visitor.
entry_documents.interaction: No entry statute targets gender expression, so the undocumented border stage is an open question rather than a shown constraint.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: The penal execution regime bars discrimination only on sexual orientation; a trans detainee has no gender-identity-specific safeguard on its face, and placement practice is unaddressed.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No anti-trans statute, arrest pattern or police targeting is recorded; no trans detention case appears in the sources.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody rules would default to birth-sex arrangements absent a gender-identity clause, but no instance is documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Reported practice diverges from policy: LGBTI people are described as often verbally abused and discriminated against in some public services, medical centres among them.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No law bars trans people from public facilities, health care or employment; 2022 health-system amendment requires non-discriminatory policy on gender identity; 2024 decrees impose confidentiality of gender identity on GBV and protection staff.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility access is not restricted by rule; the friction sits at staff discretion, with no documented remedy invoked by a trans person.

care_services.exposure: Verbal abuse and discrimination in some medical centres documented; no source shows enforcement of the non-discrimination guarantees in a case involving a transgender person.
care_services.protection: Health policy must be non-discriminatory on gender identity; social workers barred from discriminating and from disclosing gender identity without authorisation.
care_services.interaction: A paper guarantee operating against divergent frontline practice, with confidentiality duties the strongest concrete safeguard for a visitor.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Hate-crime aggravation and sectoral non-discrimination clauses cover sexual orientation only; no general anti-discrimination law reaches gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No state threat-framing: senior officials endorse the annual Pride march, the head of government televised support in 2017 and the head of state backed the 2019 event; no criminalisation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Institutional acceptance coexists with statutory gaps, so officials are unlikely to be the source of harm but recourse is thin.

minors_guardians.exposure: Transgender students recorded as more likely to be bullied and to drop out; corrective rape, forced-marriage attempts and family abuse documented against trans men and LBT women.
minors_guardians.protection: 2024 decree requires children's access to protection services regardless of gender, names trans children as at greater risk and binds case managers to respond by gender identity; 2023 law bars discrimination based on gender.
minors_guardians.interaction: Strong paper protection for minors, unproven in enforcement; no documented state barrier for an accompanying guardian.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Harassment, discrimination and family/community-based violence documented; a 57-person self-selected 2017 survey reports 86% violence but is not a population rate; hostile messages sent to the 2017 organiser's family.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Physical abuse in public or by public authorities described as uncommon; domestic violence law covers intimate relationships regardless of gender; no police targeting recorded.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence is community- and family-based rather than state-directed, and the non-discrimination police decrees have no documented trans enforcement.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No gender-identity hate-crime or general non-discrimination coverage; partnership recognition closed, and no source shows a partner read as same-sex obtaining residence, next-of-kin standing or medical decision-making.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Domestic violence law treats those living in conditions analogous to spouses as family without cohabitation; decrees create confidentiality and non-discrimination duties on service staff.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: The partner question is unresolved rather than documented as refusal; protection instruments are recent and untested for trans complainants.

anchor_checks.comparison: Kestrel Isles documents actual entry friction: extended secondary screening, discretionary refusals and return transport for document/presentation divergence. Here no border screening, refusal or luggage-search pattern is documented at all, and no public-order ground is available to refuse a trans visitor. That places this dossier materially above that anchor, with the border stage an open question rather than a shown administrative harm.

Vellmaris has national equality law expressly protecting gender identity, courts reliably ordering release and a complaint board granting apology and compensation. This dossier has comparable institutional acceptance (official Pride endorsement) but no gender-identity equality statute and no documented remedy working for a trans complainant, so it sits a little below — tier-5 paper protection against tier-3 everyday hostility.

Meridia documents trained border officers, written reasons for detention, tribunal appeals and compensation for unlawful holding. None of that machinery is documented here for gender identity; the non-discrimination decrees are sexual-orientation-only and unenforced in any trans case. This dossier therefore falls clearly below that anchor despite the absence of any criminalisation or entry bar.

Vesskar couples biometric identity checks with a public-order statute penalising deceptive presentation, producing routine exposure, detention for verification and denial of care. This dossier has no such statute, no linked biometric checkpoint regime and no documented prosecution or verification detention, so it stands well above that anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is one of legal silence plus institutional welcome, not restriction. Nothing in entry, facilities, custody text or policing criminalises or systematically exposes a trans visitor, and the executive has publicly embraced Pride. What a visitor actually meets is social friction hardening into hostility in places — verbal abuse in some public services including clinics, family and community violence, bullying of trans students — with no gender-identity hate-crime or general non-discrimination coverage and no documented case in which the sectoral protections were enforced for a trans person. Family-based rather than state-based violence limits a lone tourist's exposure but not a visitor staying with relatives. Recent 2024 decrees naming trans people are a genuine documented positive, untested in practice.
